results.title: Google TurboQuant — Paper, Tools, Benchmarks & Framework Status
results.content:
## When TurboQuant matters most

1

### Long-context serving

RAG pipelines, document Q&A, and multi-turn chat at 32k–128k tokens per request. KV cache is the dominant memory cost at these lengths.

2

### Batch inference at scale

Serving multiple concurrent requests where KV cache memory limits batch size. Reducing cache per request means more concurrent users per GPU.

3

### Consumer GPU deployment [...] Decoder models cache attention keys and values so they do not recompute the full prefix at every step. As context grows, this cache dominates GPU memory — often more than the model weights themselves at 128k+ contexts.

KV cache memory formula

2 × kv\_heads × head\_dim × layers × context\_len × batch × bytes

A single Llama 3.1 70B request at 128k context in FP16 needs an estimated ~40 GB just for KV cache (based on the KV formula). At a 3-bit target, TurboQuant would reduce that to ~7.5 GB. [...] How much memory does TurboQuant save?+

Google reports at least 6× KV cache memory reduction compared to FP16. For example, Llama 3.1 70B at 128k context drops from ~40 GB to ~7.5 GB of KV cache memory.

How does TurboQuant compare to KIVI?+

TurboQuant achieves higher quality at similar compression rates. At 3.5 bits, TurboQuant matches FP16 quality (Needle score 0.997), while KIVI at 2-bit is more aggressive but scores 0.981. TurboQuant also provides up to 8× attention speedup on H100.

results.title: Google's TurboQuant: The Compression Breakthrough ...
results.content:
The most immediate application is extending what a given GPU allocation can support for long-context inference. If your KV cache at 128K tokens was consuming 24 GB, TurboQuant brings that down to around 4 GB. That means either serving longer contexts on the same hardware, or packing more concurrent users onto each GPU.

## Get Akshay Kalane’s stories in your inbox

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. [...] Every time a decoder-based transformer generates a new token, it stores a key vector and a value vector for that token across every attention layer. That collection of vectors is the model’s working memory for the current conversation. And it grows linearly with context length. Running a 70-billion-parameter model for 512 concurrent users can burn through 512 GB of cache memory alone, nearly four times what the model weights themselves consume. [...] Running LLMs on consumer hardware (phones, laptops, edge devices) is severely memory-constrained. A 3-bit KV cache can make 32K+ context windows feasible on devices with 8–16 GB of RAM, where a full-precision cache simply would not fit. The community has already started porting TurboQuant to MLX (Apple Silicon) and llama.cpp, targeting exactly this use case.

results.content:
Let me start with a number. Running a 70B parameter model for 128 concurrent users at 32K context consumes roughly 2.6TB of KV cache memory. That’s HBM on your GPUs, the scarcest and most expensive resource in your inference stack. An H100 gives you 80GB of it. Even the B200, NVIDIA’s current flagship, tops out at 192GB. You can do the math on how many cards you need just to hold the memory of past conversations before you’ve done a single FLOP of actual computation. [...] ### Summary

TurboQuant is a new compression algorithm from Google Research that delivers 5X KV cache compression with near-zero accuracy loss, freeing scarce GPU memory so LLMs can support longer contexts, more users, and bigger models on existing infrastructure.

image_pdfimage_print [...] First, you can run bigger models on the same GPUs. The KV cache pre-allocation that used to crowd out model weights now takes a fraction of the space. A model that previously required eight GPUs to serve at 32K context might fit on four. Better results, new capabilities, no hardware upgrade. Same results, half the cluster.

results.title: Why TurboQuant matters for real-world LLM inference
results.content: The practical promise of TurboQuant is simple: more useful context capacity on the same hardware. If KV-cache memory shrinks substantially while model quality stays stable on the reported benchmarks, a serving stack can fit more active sessions per GPU, support longer contexts, or postpone an infrastructure upgrade. [...] In production, the KV cache is often the first scaling problem that really hurts. As prompts get longer, chats persist across many turns, or RAG systems attach more retrieved context to every request, KV-cache memory grows quickly and starts limiting concurrency, latency, and infrastructure efficiency. [...] Use TurboQuant when serving Llama 3 or Llama 3.1 Instruct with long context and many concurrent chats, where KV-cache memory starts limiting how many sessions a single GPU can sustain. In that setting, the goal is not only to save memory, but to keep long histories practical without moving too early to a larger GPU tier.

## TurboQuant เป็นผู้นำในด้านตัวชี้วัดผลการดำเนินงาน

TurboQuant ของ Google ประสบความสำเร็จในด้านประสิทธิภาพและการบีบอัดที่ก้าวล้ำ โดยสามารถบีบอัดข้อมูลเวกเตอร์ขนาด 32 บิต หรือ 16 บิต ให้เหลือเพียงประมาณ 3 บิต ด้วยอัตราการบีบอัดที่สูงถึง 6 เท่า ซึ่งช่วยลดการใช้พื้นที่หน่วยความจำของ KV Cache ในโมเดลขนาดใหญ่ลงเหลือเพียงหนึ่งในหกของระดับเดิมได้โดยตรง [...] TurboQuant เป็นอัลกอริทึมการบีบอัดเวกเตอร์ (vector compression) ใหม่ที่เปิดตัวอย่างเป็นทางการโดย Google Research ในเดือนมีนาคม 2026 โดยมีเป้าหมายเพื่อแก้ปัญหาสำคัญในขั้นตอนการประมวลผล (inference) ของโมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญ่ (LLMs) และเครื่องมือค้นหาเวกเตอร์ (vector search engines) นั่นคือการใช้หน่วยความจำมหาศาลของ Key-Value Cache (KV Cache) ทั้งนี้ รายละเอียดทางเทคนิคจะถูกเผยแพร่อย่างเป็นทางการและผ่านการพิจารณาโดยผู้ทรงคุณวุฒิในรูปแบบของบทความวิชาการในงาน ICLR 2026 (International Conference on [...] เป้าหมายการเพิ่มประสิทธิภาพของ TurboQuant ถูกล็อกไว้ที่โมดูล KV cache และดัชนีเวกเตอร์ (vector index) อย่างแม่นยำ ซึ่งเป็นส่วนประกอบที่ใช้หน่วยความจำมากที่สุดในสถานการณ์การประมวลผล (Inference) AI เมื่อเทคโนโลยีนี้ถูกนำมาใช้งานในวงกว้าง เซิร์ฟเวอร์เพียงเครื่องเดียวจะมีความสามารถในการ "รองรับโมเดลได้มากขึ้นโดยใช้หน่วยความจำน้อยลง" สิ่งนี้ได้กระตุ้นความกังวลในตลาดว่าอัตราการเติบโตของความต้องการความจุ DRAM อาจชะลอตัวลง ซึ่งเป็นสาเหตุโดยตรงของการเปลี่ยนแปลงบรรยากาศในตลาดเมื่อเร็ว ๆ นี้

results.title: What TurboQuant Actually Means for AI Memory Stocks
results.content:
Google's TurboQuant targets something called the Key-Value (KV) cache – the working memory AI models use to store contextual information so they don't have to recompute it with every new token they generate. As models process longer inputs, the KV cache grows rapidly, consuming GPU memory at an alarming rate. TurboQuant compresses that cache from 16 bits per value down to just 3 bits – a 6x reduction in memory footprint – with, per Google's benchmarks, zero loss in model accuracy. No retraining [...] TurboQuant, if widely adopted, compresses the KV cache by 6x. So the bearish argument goes that if the KV cache is 6x smaller, we'll need 6x less memory.

'Memory demand – and memory stocks – will crater. Sell everything.'

Wells Fargo (WFC) analyst Andrew Rocha articulated this cleanly: if TurboQuant is adopted broadly, it quickly raises the question of how much memory capacity the industry actually needs.

That's a fair question. It's just that the answer isn't what the bears think.

results.title: What Is Google TurboQuant Compression Algorithm? How Does It Affect the AI Memory Chip Industry?
results.content:
Industry consensus indicates that the current bottleneck for large models is not the number of parameters but memory capacity. The longer the context, the larger the memory footprint of the KV Cache, which eventually hits hardware limits before the model parameters do. This is a shared pain point for tasks such as long-text generation and long-document understanding.

TurboQuant's breakthrough directly addresses this pain point. [...] In inference scenarios, HBM actually stands to gain additional benefits from TurboQuant. With a 6x compression ratio, the technology significantly reduces KV cache occupancy per GPU, effectively increasing the number of concurrent requests a GPU can process. The bandwidth advantages of HBM, which were previously limited by KV cache capacity, can now be more fully unleashed. The resulting improvement in actual inference efficiency will further strengthen HBM's deployment value in high-end AI [...] TurboQuant's optimization targets are precisely locked on the KV cache and vector index modules, which are the most memory-intensive components in AI inference scenarios. Once the technology is deployed at scale, a single server will gain the ability to "host more models with less memory." This has triggered market concerns that the growth rate of demand for DRAM capacity may slow down, which is the direct cause of the recent shift in market sentiment.
